comparisons.peer_summary: AMD collaborates with industry leaders and open-source initiatives on early-stage R&D and conducts product/system R&D primarily in the United States, supplemented by engineering teams in various other countries directing specific activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD explicitly highlight their contributions to open-source software initiatives as part of their broader open platform or R&D strategy. Intel states it has 'contributed to the design, build, and validation of open-source products in the industry such as Linux, Android, and others' to support its open platforms. Similarly, AMD notes it is 'actively contributing to numerous industry open-source software initiatives across a broad range of technologies' while collaborating with industry leaders on R&D.

sentences.text: We also contributed to the design, build, and validation of open-source products in the industry such as Linux, Android, and others.

We also work with industry leaders on process technology, design tools, intellectual property, software and other industry consortia to conduct early-stage R&D. We are also actively contributing to numerous industry open-source software initiatives across a broad range of technologies.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's AI strategy is focused on three priorities: delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions, expanding ecosystem partnerships to accelerate deployments, and providing compelling user experiences via the open ROCm software platform.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies define their strategic priorities around the delivery of open platforms and software ecosystems. Intel aims to 'deliver open software and hardware platforms with industry-defining standards.' AMD similarly identifies an 'open and proven software platform' as the third priority of its AI strategy, enabling its hardware to be deployed broadly. While Intel focuses on historical industry standards (CXL, PCIe), AMD emphasizes the extensibility of its ROCm software platform for AI workloads.

sentences.text: We aim to deliver open software and hardware platforms with industry-defining standards.
And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom provides Ethernet NICs, switching, and routing products optimized for AI data centers and service provider networks, focusing on high capacity, low latency, and scalability.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom describe their networking solutions as being based on open, standards-based protocols, specifically Ethernet. Intel notes that companies build networks on 'open standards-based platforms,' implying the ubiquity of these standards. Broadcom explicitly describes its products as offering an 'enhanced, open, standards-based Ethernet network interface card ("NIC")' to resolve connectivity bottlenecks, aligning with the industry shift toward open standards in data center infrastructure.

sentences.text: Around the globe, companies are building their networks, systems, and solutions on open standards-based platforms.

Our products offer an enhanced, open, standards-based Ethernet network interface card ("NIC") and switching solution to resolve connectivity bottlenecks in data centers, particularly in AI data centers where compute bandwidth and cluster sizes grow rapidly.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Compute and Networking Business Unit includes memory products and solutions for data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets, including HBM, DDR, LPDRAM, GDDR, CXL, and MRDIMM.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Micron both reference Composable Acceleration Link (CXL) as a key technology within their open standard or product portfolio contributions. Intel cites its historic contributions to developing standards such as 'CXL' as part of its open platform strategy. Micron lists 'compute express link ("CXL")' as an emerging memory technology included in its Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU) portfolio.

sentences.text: We have helped set the stage for this movement, with our historic contributions in developing standards such as CXL, Thunderbolt™, and PCI Express.

CNBU includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets including HBM, DDR, LPDRAM and GDDR, as well as some emerging memory technologies like compute express link ("CXL") and multi-ranked dual in-line memory module ("MRDIMM").
